section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design
text: ABSTRACT: To understand the efects of additives on the performance of a Ni− Co−P alloy electroplated coating, this study, based on a single-factor experiment, utilized a Box−Behnken experimental design to optimize an additive that can enhance the electrodeposited Ni−Co−P alloy coating’s properties, including hardness, glossiness, and corrosion resistance. The study used tools such as a gloss meter, a Vickers hardness tester, and an electrochemical workstation to analyze the impact of diferent additives on the coating’s hardness and gloss. The optimal additive combination was determined.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design
text: The study used tools such as a gloss meter, a Vickers hardness tester, and an electrochemical workstation to analyze the impact of diferent additives on the coating’s hardness and gloss. The optimal additive combination was determined. The results from the Box−Behnken experiment showed that when the concentrations of sodium dodecyl sulfate, thiourea, and sodium allyl sulfonate reached 0.10, 0.15, and 0.22 g/L, respectively, the resulting coating hardness was 475.4 HV _0.5, and the gloss level was 463.4 GU.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 1. INTRODUCTION
text: Chrome plating has been highly favored for its advantages (e.g., high hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and wear resistance), whereas the environmental pollution and health hazards arising from hexavalent chromium in the plating solution have aroused rising attention. 1,2 Electroplated Ni− Co−P alloy coatings have been considered a promising alternative to chrome plating for their prominent thermal stability, corrosion resistance, and wear resistance, as reported in existing research.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 1. INTRODUCTION
text: 1,2 Electroplated Ni− Co−P alloy coatings have been considered a promising alternative to chrome plating for their prominent thermal stability, corrosion resistance, and wear resistance, as reported in existing research. 3−6 However, several problems (e.g., severe hydrogen evolution at the cathode and unstable plating solution) during the electroplating process of Ni−W−B alloy coatings can trigger cracked coatings, lack of metallic luster, and inadequate decorative properties. 7,8 Accordingly, the electroplating process of the Ni−W−B alloy should be investigated in depth.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 1. INTRODUCTION
text: The efects of additives on _Ni-Co-P coatings in electroplating have rarely been investigated. In this study, the preliminary screening of surfactants and brighteners was conducted through single-factor experiments based on the basic formulation of the electroplated Ni−Co−P alloy. RSM was employed to design experiments and investigate the efects of additives ( e.g., SDS, thiourea, and ALS) on the hardness and glossiness of the coatings. Stable plating solutions and coatings with excellent performance were obtained through compre hensive analysis and optimization.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 1. INTRODUCTION
text: Stable plating solutions and coatings with excellent performance were obtained through compre hensive analysis and optimization. This study aimed at providing more insights into the efects of process conditions and plating solution composition on the coating performance. It can lay a solid basis for in-depth research on N i - C o - P and its composite coatings while providing a useful reference for the industrial production of electroplated Ni−Co−P compo site coatings.

text: 4.1. Single-Factor Experiments. 4.1.1. Efect of Surfactant on Coating Hardness. The addition of the surfactant SDS to the plating solution was investigated to determine its efect on coating performance. The results, shown in Figure 1, indicate that as the SDS concentration increased, the porosity of the coating decreased and the hardness increased. When the SDS concentration reached 0.1 g / L, the coating exhibited the lowest porosity of 0.23 pores/ cm ^2 and the maximum hardness of 4 0 8.4 HV _0.5.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 4. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
text: When the SDS concentration reached 0.1 g / L, the coating exhibited the lowest porosity of 0.23 pores/ cm ^2 and the maximum hardness of 4 0 8.4 HV _0.5. However, further increasing the SDS concentration led to an increase in coating porosity and a decrease in hardness. The appropriate addition of SDS facilitated the forward shift of the nucleation potential and reduced cathodic polarization during deposition, 19 which can contribute to coating formation.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 4. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
text: The appropriate addition of SDS facilitated the forward shift of the nucleation potential and reduced cathodic polarization during deposition, 19 which can contribute to coating formation. Moreover, it lowered the surface tension of the plating solution, thus facilitating the easy release of hydrogen gas generated during the hydrogen evolution reaction on the cathode surface. Thus, the formation of pinholes and pitting was reduced, resulting in a lower coating porosity and a denser coating structure, leading to an increase in hardness.

text: Thus, the formation of pinholes and pitting was reduced, resulting in a lower coating porosity and a denser coating structure, leading to an increase in hardness. However, excessive surfactant concentration can cause the aggregation of surfactant molecules, forming micelles, thus afecting the deposition process and resulting in decreased coating hardness and increased porosity.

A larger capacitive arc radius can represent a larger charge-transfer resistance, suggesting greater dificulty in charge-transfer and better corrosion resistance of the material. 28 It can be clearly identified that the addition of additives to the plating bath resulted in a significant increase in the capacitive arc radius of the coating, suggesting improved corrosion resistance.

section: Study on the Efects of Additives on the Performance of Ni−Co−P Alloy Coatings Using Box−Behnken Design > 5. CONCLUSIONS
text: Through the Box−Behnken experiment for additive formula tion, the optimal additive combination was determined to be an SDS concentration of 0.10 g/L, thiourea concentration of 0.15 g/L, and ALS concentration of 0.22 g / L. The coatings obtained under these optimized additive conditions exhibited a hardness of 4 7 5.4 HV _0.5, which was 9 0.3 4 HV _0.5 higher than that of the coating without additives. The glossiness of the coating was 463.4GU, which increased by 101.2GU compared with the coating without additives. The corrosion resistance of the coatings was also improved.

The addition of additives improved the surface morphology of the coatings, making them smoother and more compact. The addition of the optimized additive combination significantly improved the coating performance, resulting in coatings with a metallic luster similar to stainless steel, which meets industrial requirements.
